title: Carrier-Resolved Attosecond Valley Polarimetry of Monolayer MoS$_2$
authors: Navdeep Rana, Lun Yue, Mette B. Gaarde
abstract: In recent years, all-optical writing and switching of valley polarization in two-dimensional semiconductors has been demonstrated on femtosecond timescales. Reading this polarization out on the same timescale, carrier by carrier, has so far remained out of reach. Employing semiconductor Bloch equation simulations of monolayer MoS$_2$, we show that attosecond transient absorption closes this gap by turning the Mo $4p$ semicore edge into a quantitative valley polarimeter. We find that pump-enabled core-to-valence absorption probes the holes while core-to-conduction bleaching probes the electrons, so that a single spectrum identifies each carrier by its photoabsorption energy. The hole channel, Pauli-blocked in equilibrium, emerges background-free. Its circular dichroism reverses sign with the pump helicity, and its normalized magnitude is proportional to the valley polarization. Finally, we show that scanning the probe delay clocks the few-femtosecond write in real time. Thus, attosecond core-level dichroism is a carrier-sensitive, quantitative probe of the creation and evolution of valley polarization.
summary: This work demonstrates that attosecond transient absorption spectroscopy can serve as a quantitative, carrier-resolved polarimeter for measuring valley polarization in monolayer MoS2. By analyzing the circular dichroism at the Mo 4p core edge, the authors can track the creation and evolution of valley polarization in real time, providing a powerful tool for ultrafast valleytronics research.
main_problem: The core challenge is developing a method to read out valley polarization (VP) in 2D semiconductors on the same ultrafast timescale (attosecond) that it can be written or switched.
main_result: Attosecond transient absorption spectroscopy (ATA) successfully functions as a carrier-sensitive, quantitative polarimeter, allowing the real-time tracking of valley polarization buildup and dynamics.
method: The study combines theoretical simulations using semiconductor Bloch equations with the concept of attosecond core-level dichroism measurements.
model_or_system: The system is monolayer MoS2, a 2D semiconductor whose valley pseudospin is probed using the Mo 4p semicore edge. The theory employs a tight-binding model solved via semiconductor Bloch equations.
key_observables: Circular Dichroism (CD) of the transient absorption spectrum ($\Delta\mu_{\pm}$), which is shown to be linearly proportional to the valley polarization (VP).
important_parameters: Attosecond probe delay (time resolution), pump helicity ($\sigma^\pm$), and the energy separation between hole ($\approx 35.0 	ext{ eV}$) and electron ($\approx 38.5 	ext{ eV}$) transitions.
main_assumptions: The simulation assumes the core semicore level is localized on Mo atoms and neglects population relaxation, though the symmetry rules are robust.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the readout scheme, showing how $\sigma^+$ and $\sigma^-$ probes yield different signals, and demonstrate the time evolution of the hole-line CD tracking the valley population buildup.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for ultrafast readout, details the use of ATA and core-level transitions to separate electron/hole signals, presents the quantitative relationship between CD and VP, and finally demonstrates time-resolved tracking of the valley dynamics.
why_interesting: The methodology of using core-level transitions to create a highly sensitive, background-free, and carrier-resolved probe for non-equilibrium quantum states (valley polarization) is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics.
